original_question: Suppose F is a factor, that is, an invariant sub-sigma-algebra, for the ergodic product system T tensor T, and suppose F is independent of the two coordinate sigma-algebras. Must the entropy of the automorphism T then be positive?
target_in_paper: §2, Q10 ("Independent factor"), stated immediately after Q9 as a very special case of the del Junco–Rudolph entropy problem.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper’s Q10 almost verbatim: a factor for the product system T⊗T, independence from the two coordinate factors, and the question whether this forces positive entropy of T.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: T is a measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space (X, B, μ).
The product system is specifically the product automorphism T⊗T acting on (X×X, B⊗B, μ⊗μ), and the paper explicitly says this product is ergodic.
The factor F should be identified as a T⊗T-invariant sub-σ-algebra of B⊗B.
The 'two coordinate sigma-algebras' should be spelled out as the first and second coordinate factors, i.e. B⊗{∅,X} and {∅,X}⊗B.
The entropy meant is the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy h(T).
The paper places this question as a special case of the broader Q9 on zero-entropy weakly mixing automorphisms failing the properties S_n; that contextual scope is implicit in your draft.
No additional algebraic data such as ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers are relevant in this ergodic-theory problem.
refined_question: Let T be a measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space (X, B, μ), and assume that the product automorphism T⊗T on (X×X, B⊗B, μ⊗μ) is ergodic. Suppose there exists a T⊗T-invariant factor F ⊆ B⊗B that is independent of each of the two coordinate factors B⊗{∅,X} and {∅,X}⊗B. Must the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy h(T) be positive?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Q10 in §2. The paper introduces Q9 as the del Junco–Rudolph problem about zero-entropy weakly mixing automorphisms failing S_n, then says that the 'independent factor' question is a very particular unresolved case of that problem, namely Q10. Your draft matches Q10 closely, but it leaves implicit the probability-space setting, the exact product action T⊗T, the ergodicity of that product, the precise meaning of the coordinate factors, and the fact that the entropy is h(T). The nearby Theorem 2.3 gives only a special sufficient case: when F is generated by the set (A×A)∪(A^c×A^c) with μ(A)=1/2, the factor is Bernoulli, yielding positive entropy; this sharpens the local context but is not presented as an equivalent reformulation. So the faithful refinement is to restate Q10 itself, not the broader Q9 and not a generalized variant.
